title: Final Fantasy XV Took Ten Years and Two Names to Come Out
hook:
Final Fantasy XV was announced in May 2006 as Versus XIII and did not ship until November 2016, then moved 5 million copies in a single day. Was it worth the ten year wait for you?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Final Fantasy Fifteen took more than ten years to come out? It was first announced at E3 in May of two thousand six, but not under that name. Back then it was called Final Fantasy Versus Thirteen, a PlayStation Three exclusive spinoff of Final Fantasy Thirteen, with Tetsuya Nomura directing. Then it mostly vanished. Years went by with barely a trailer, and fans started to wonder if it would ever ship. The wait ended up outlasting an entire console generation. At E3 in June of two thousand thirteen, Square Enix played a Versus Thirteen trailer and then swapped out the logo. The game was now Final Fantasy Fifteen, headed to PlayStation Four and Xbox One. In September of two thousand fourteen, Hajime Tabata took over as director so Nomura could focus on Kingdom Hearts Three. Final Fantasy Fifteen finally launched in late November of two thousand sixteen, more than ten years after that first reveal. It shipped five million copies on its first day, which made it the fastest selling Final Fantasy ever at that point. Not bad for a game that spent a decade changing names, consoles and directors. Follow for more gaming history.
